subject: Post-demo: ops-ready engine choices and cost/latency impacts
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Elise Martin <elise@lumencorp.com>, Paul Gomez <paul@lumencorp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: ops-ready engine choices and cost/latency impacts

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation and helpful signal on where Lumencorp needs predictable latency and tight cost controls for search-assist and summarization. Below is a concise recap and an ops-ready shortlist with tradeoffs so your engineers and procurement can align quickly.

Quick recap
- Primary POC scope: search-assist (low-latency token streaming) + paragraph summarization (higher quality over longer context).
- Key constraints: 99th pct latency <= 220ms on tail for search-assist; per-1M-token cost target $10–$18 depending on accuracy/throughput; SOC2 + data-retention proof required for procurement.

Recommended shortlist (ops-ready picks) — rationale and expected unit impacts
1) Redwood-RT-3.7Q (quantized) — balanced
   - Why: best mix of real-time tail latency and token-cost when quantized; strong on instruction-following with our prompt-set.
   - Expected: median latency ~90–120ms (g4dn-like), 99th pct ~180–220ms with continuous batching; cost ~ $12–$15 / 1k tokens equivalent in pipeline.
   - Risk: slight drop in edge-case summarization fidelity vs FP16; mitigations: targeted prompt calibration and small prompt-aware caching.

2) Redwood-Large-7B (FP16) — quality-first
   - Why: higher fidelity on multi-paragraph summarization, fewer hallucinations on domain taxonomy.
   - Expected: median latency ~140–200ms, 99th ~300–380ms on same infra; cost ~ $20–$25 / 1k tokens.
   - Risk: misses latency SLO for search-assist at peak; fallback plan: use as async summarizer and keep RT-3.7Q for interactive.

3) Redwood-Edge-4.2 (compact) — cost-optimized
   - Why: lowest running cost for high QPS scenarios; good for high-volume short prompts (search rank re-rank).
   - Expected: median latency ~60–100ms, 99th ~150–220ms; cost ~ $9–$12 / 1k tokens.
   - Risk: quality hit on long-form summarization; acceptable for search-assist use-case.

Attachments & links
- Attached: prompt pack (lumencorp_prompt_set_v1.zip), bench summary (bench_summary_080228.csv), pilot config draft (pilot_config_draft.docx).
- Benchmarks and replay deck: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB-Redwood/lumencorp-benchmarks

Next steps (proposed, please confirm)
1) Lumencorp: confirm priority order (search-assist top priority?) and provide up to 500 redacted sample prompts for bench replay.
2) Redwood: run targeted 24h latency replay on RT-3.7Q and Edge-4.2 (we'll share the raw CSV + percentile breakdown).
3) Commercial: we’ll prepare pilot pricing for 6 weeks (incl. ingress/outbound costs) and a SOC2 evidence pack for procurement.

If that aligns, we can lock the pilot config and produce an ops-ready runbook (rollback, KV cache ops, autoscale warm-up).

Thanks — Karthik

--

Date: Thu, 2 Aug 2028 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: ops-ready engine choices and cost/latency impacts

Karthik — thanks, this is very helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our side before we hand to infra/procurement:

1) For search-assist, our product team says 99th pct <= 220ms is firm. Is RT-3.7Q reliably under that at peak? What assumptions on batching and QPS should we share with infra?
2) For the FP16 option: how disruptive is running a mixed fleet (RT-3.7Q for interactive, 7B FP16 for summaries) operationally? We want to avoid two separate vendor contracts if possible.
3) Procurement: can you expedite SOC2 artifacts and a short note on data retention/purge controls?

We’ll try to get the 500 sample prompts to you by EOD Friday.

— Elise
Elise Martin
Head of Product, Lumencorp
elise@lumencorp.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Elise Martin <elise@lumencorp.com>, Paul Gomez <paul@lumencorp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Aug 2028 13:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: ops-ready engine choices and cost/latency impacts

Elise — quick answers, and I’ve attached the initial bench CSV + prompt pack for replay.

1) RT-3.7Q latency assumptions - We validated on our standard g4dn-like profile at 500RPS sustained with continuous batching windows tuned to the request distribution you showed. Under those conditions we saw 99th ~190–210ms. If your peak bursts exceed 1k RPS, tail can degrade; mitigation: burst pool + prioritization route (we can book a short infra call to size this).

2) Mixed fleet operations - It's common. Redwood’s routing policy can run both models behind a logical route name; you can pin model for specific endpoints (e.g., /summarize -> 7B FP16) while /search-assist -> RT-3.7Q. Single commercial contract is possible (hosted or dedicated), but it does affect committed capacity and pricing tiers. We’ll coordinate plan with Ben on the commercial side.

3) SOC2 & retention - Ben/Marissa: I attached the SOC2 attestation packet and a short retention summary in the Drive link. We can produce a trimmed evidence pack for procurement next-day once they confirm scope.

Pilot ask - If Lumencorp can share the 500 prompts, we’ll run a controlled replay overnight and return per-prompt deltas, 50/90/99 percentiles, and a small prompt-calibration guide.

Deliverables timeline (if approved) - Night 0: ingest prompts and run replay (24h).
- Day 1: deliver raw CSV + percentile summary and recommended model (RT-3.7Q by default).
- Day 3: pilot config + runbook + commercial proposal.

Sharing attachments now.

Thanks, Karthik
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Subject: Lumencorp commercial note + procurement prep

Karthik / Marissa — quick internal follow:

- Commercial: I recommend we propose a 6-week pilot at a 10% pilot discount with a clear conversion path to committed Dedicated capacity. That helps procurement and gives us runway to validate tail behavior.
- Procurement pack: compile the SOC2 attestation, retention statement, and a one-page data-flow diagram — include Karthik’s expected 99th pct numbers.
- Ask: Karthik, get the replay CSV and percentile breakdown into the HubSpot deal record (link in metadata). I’ll draft the pilot SOW and a light amendment for SOC obligations.

Marissa: can you pull the standard SOC2 evidence subset for pilot (last 12 months), and I’ll DM the pricing bands we should offer?

Ben
